mentions.name: VentureStaking
mentions.description: VentureStaking is a game of startup discovery in which multiple people come together to form a grant for a founder (no debt, no equity) to spend a year researching a problem, similar to a Thiel Fellowship. If the founder discovers something interesting, the grantors can invest up to 10x their grant amount in an equity round — e.g., a $100,000 grant creates a potential $1MM equity round — letting a staker give $10 grants to 100 founders and invest 10x in the few that discover great opportunities. SEC rules are triggered only at the first equity round, with RegCF allowing multiple retail investors as one line item on the cap table.
mentions.problem: Because 9 out of 10 startups fail, early startup investing is not investing but philanthropy with a potential upside.
mentions.audience: Founders who receive the grants and VentureStakers/retail investors who pool small grants and follow on in the most promising founders.
mentions.source_excerpt: So I’ve created a new game of Venture call VentureStaking where multiple people come together to form a grant for a founder (no debt / no equity) to spend a year researching a problem (ie Thiel Fellowship) and then if that founder discovers something interesting, the grantors can invest up to 10x their grant amount in equity.
